title: Error messages and microcopy

body.text: A good error message answers 3 questions:
what happened · why · what to do next
— 'Error 500' is a UX failure, while 'Couldn't save because the connection dropped. Try again.' is good work.

example: "Rewrite the error: 'Invalid input' → 'Phone number must be 10 digits and start with 0, e.g. 0812345678'"

title: Microcopy at the critical points

body.text: the sign-up form (reduce anxiety) · the payment button (build confidence) · the empty state (show the first step)
— have Claude write several versions per point, then pick by brand tone.

example: "Under the email field in the sign-up form, write 3 anxiety-reducing microcopy options, e.g. 'No spam, unsubscribe anytime'"

question: What questions should a good error message answer?

options.text: What happened, why, what to do next

question: Which is a good error message?

options.text: "Phone number must be 10 digits starting with 0"

question: What kind of microcopy should an empty state have?

options.text: Tell the first step the user should take

question: What should a good error message do?

options.text: State the cause and the fix in a friendly tone

question: What does microcopy at critical points help with?

options.text: Reduces confusion and builds the user's confidence
